newsitem.title: USA: Boston Market expanding to China, Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: Boston Market expanding to China, Taiwan.

text.p: Home-style American cooking is going to Asia.

Boston Chicken Inc. said Wednesday that a new company formed to franchise Boston Market stores outside the United States had signed a letter of intent to open 600 stores in China and Taiwan over the next decade.
The agreement marks the first time that Boston Market stores, which specialise in quick, home-style American meals, will expand overseas.

The announcement said the new company, Boston Market International Inc., signed the letter of intent with John Sun, an experienced restaurateur with expertise in bringing American restaurants to Asia.
It said Sun was involved in the development and operation of McDonald's restaurants in Taiwan and China between 1983 and 1994 and currently operates TGI Friday's restaurants in Taiwan and Beijing.
Sun will serve as chairman and chief executive of a new company to which Boston Market International will franchise rights to develop and operate Boston Market stores.
The new Taiwan-based company will be funded with about $20 million in capital from Sun and other private investors and a $60 million convertible loan from Boston Market International.
Boston Market International will have the option to convert its loan into a majority equity interest in the Taiwan company at a later date, it said.
The announcement said Boston Chicken was licensing to Boston Market International the rights to use the Boston Market brand in Taiwan and China.

Boston Market International, in turn, is expected to be funded initially with private equity capital and with a convertible loan from Boston Chicken, which will have the option to convert the loan into a majority equity interest at a later date.
Saad Nadhir, co-chairman of Boston Chicken, is spearheading the company's overseas expansion. Nadhir headed the international development of Blockbuster Video.
"We've always believed the Boston Market brand has tremendous international potential," he said in a statement.
"We view this transaction as the first of many agreements with experienced, proven restaurant developers and operators all over the world."

Scott Beck, the other co-chairman of Boston Chicken, said that while the company was expanding its brand overseas, it would also continue its rapid growth in the United States, opening between 300 and 350 stores this year.
The transactions are subject to the execution of definitive agreements, expected to take place during first-quarter 1997, the announcement said.
The first international Boston Market store is expected to open in Taipei, Taiwan, late this year or early 1998. Other target cities include the Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou in China.
Boston Chicken's stock added 25 cents to $35.625 in early trading on the Nasdaq market.
